title: A weekend in Lisbon
text:
Last spring my sister and I spent three days in Lisbon. We arrived on Friday evening and took the old yellow tram to our hotel in Alfama. The streets there are narrow and steep, so we walked slowly and stopped a lot.

On Saturday we visited the castle. From the top you can see the whole city and the river. In the afternoon it started to rain, so we went to a small café and ate pastéis de nata, the famous cream cakes of the city.

On Sunday we took a train to Belém. The tower was full of tourists, but the queue moved fast. We came home tired, with a hundred photos and a plan to go back in summer.

questions.question: How long did the writer stay in Lisbon?
questions.explanation: La primera frase lo dice: «my sister and I spent three days in Lisbon».

questions.question: How did they travel to their hotel?
questions.explanation: «We arrived on Friday evening and took the old yellow tram to our hotel». Caminaron por Alfama, pero al hotel llegaron en tranvía.

questions.question: Why did they go to a café on Saturday afternoon?
questions.explanation: «In the afternoon it started to rain, so we went to a small café»: *so* introduce la consecuencia, y la causa es la lluvia.

questions.question: What does the writer say about the tower in Belém?
questions.explanation: «The tower was full of tourists, but the queue moved fast»: había mucha gente, pero la cola avanzaba rápido.

questions.question: Which city is the text about?
questions.explanation: El texto habla de Lisboa: Alfama, Belém y los pastéis de nata son barrios y dulces de la ciudad.

questions.question: What did they eat in the café?
questions.answer: Pastéis de nata / Cream cakes / Cakes
questions.explanation: «we ate pastéis de nata, the famous cream cakes of the city»: la aposición traduce el nombre portugués.
